sandbox_image.distribution: Built locally with scripts/build-sandbox.sh on 2026-11-24 from the 0.2.4 Dockerfile the tag carries. The image published to GitHub Container Registry for this release is a separate build of the same Dockerfile; its Ubuntu packages are not version-pinned and can differ (each image lists them in /usr/share/doc/oxfuzz-sandbox/packages.tsv).

scenarios_passed: Network unavailable, input read-only, explicitly mounted output writable, 256 MiB and 1 CPU cgroup limits verified
Explicit numeric UID/GID can read private input and creates correctly owned output
Running container registered with owned workspace label
Runtime ownership records inaccessible inside the sandbox
Fresh runtime cleans up container left by terminated helper client
helper: Seventh test is the recovery child-process helper, not an independent scenario.
device_policy: New in 0.9.11: the runtime accepts exactly /dev/kvm as a passthrough device, only when the host has it as a character device, and refuses any other device before Docker runs. Covered by unit and integration tests in CI; this macOS host has no /dev/kvm, so no device was passed here.

semgrep.provenance: The 0.2.4 image build runs an offline Semgrep scan with a read-only source mount and checks its report on the host. That check passed when this image was built on 2026-11-24 and again when the same image was rebuilt from cache on 2026-11-24 after the verification-mount fix; it was not repeated for this record.

limitations: Host is macOS arm64; this is not a Linux host qualification. Windows is not supported.
Docker failure recovery scenarios cover only disposable owned containers.
All seven tests reported ok (six scenarios and the recovery helper).
Only the linux/arm64 image was used here; the linux/amd64 image was built and verified by the GitHub workflow, not run through these scenarios.
candidate_delta: None known. This run was made in a separate worktree checked out at the tag commit, with no other changes in it; the engine qualification that ran in the same worktree immediately afterwards recorded an empty working-tree patch. No digest was taken for this run itself.
